name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt a rolling 30-day weighted decay with a 20% floor for prompts above 100. It balances relevance and stability better than a hard 7-day decay, which risks losing useful patterns too quickly. The 20% floor prevents critical prompts from vanishing entirely, while the weighted decay ensures newer, more active prompts dominate. Trade-off: we accept slightly slower adaptation to new trends in exchange for retaining proven high-value prompts.

name: Gauge
text: The rolling 30-day weighted decay still risks locking in stale prompts if the weights decay too slowly—critical but low-usage prompts get buried before newer ones prove their value. A hybrid model: 7-day hard decay for prompts under 100 uses, rolling 30-day weighted decay for those above, with a 10% floor, would cut both over-rotation and stagnation risks. Settle it by testing both on a 30-day slice of real usage data and comparing prompt drift metrics.
